source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
Basal fertilizer (applied at or before planting) is used to boost soil fertility and stimulate early crop growth; strong establishment in the crop's early growth stage is a major contributor to high final yield. At the seedling/germination stage, corn particularly needs phosphorus to build a strong root system and sturdy stem — a phosphorus deficiency at this stage is difficult to correct later, so phosphorus should be supplied as basal fertilizer. Nitrogen is also important for corn overall.

The recommended basal fertilizer is DAP (ជីដេអាប៊ែ). The source states DAP's nutrient content as nitrogen 18% and phosphorus 46% in the land-preparation/basal-fertilizer chapter, but later, in the plant-nutrition chapter, the same document states DAP's content as nitrogen (N) 18% and phosphorus (P2O5) 48%. Both figures were confirmed by direct visual inspection of the respective pages, so this is a genuine internal numeric discrepancy in the source document (46% vs. 48% phosphorus content) rather than a transcription error — flagged here rather than resolved.

Application method: fertilizer should be placed in the soil so that it sits below or to the side of the planted seed — seeds must not be placed in direct contact with the fertilizer, since this can cause the seed or seedling to rot.

Caution: continuous, repeated use of DAP over many years can increase soil acidity. However, not applying any additional fertilizer also degrades soil quality over time. Where possible, continuing to use natural/organic fertilizer is recommended as a way to help maintain both soil quality and the environment.
